resources.string: On the computer running your Dashboardz hub, open the admin page, go to Devices and choose Add device. It shows a QR code, the hub address and a 6-character code: scan the QR code, or type the address and code here.

Can\'t reach a hub at %1$s. Check that the hub is running, that the address and port match the admin\'s Devices page, and that this device is on the same Wi-Fi network as the hub (not a guest network).
Can\'t find %1$s on the network. Check the hub address, or use its IP address instead of a name.
%1$s accepted the connection but didn\'t answer. Check that it is your Dashboardz hub, then try again.
Couldn\'t make a secure connection to %1$s. Older Android versions don\'t trust some certificates. On your local network, try the hub\'s http:// address instead.
That code didn\'t work. Codes are 6 characters, work once and expire after 10 minutes. Create a new one on the hub\'s Devices page.
Pairing codes are 6 characters: letters and the digits 2 to 9. They never contain 0, 1, I or O, so check the code and try again.
Something answered at %1$s, but it isn\'t a Dashboardz hub. Check the address and port (the hub uses 8484 unless you changed it).
The hub ran into a problem (HTTP %1$d). Try again in a moment, or check the hub\'s logs.
That doesn\'t look like a hub address. It should look like 192.168.1.20:8484.
%1$s only works on the hub\'s own computer, not from this device. Type the hub computer\'s network address instead (like 192.168.1.20:8484). To fix the QR code, set PUBLIC_URL on the hub.
This device was removed from the hub. Create a new code on the hub\'s Devices page to pair it again.
That QR code isn\'t a pairing code
Pairing failed. Check the hub address and the code, then try again.
For when the hub\'s IP address or name changed. This device stays paired. To connect to a different hub, unpair this device instead.
The screen never sleeps. Turn off to let it sleep normally; critical alerts wake it either way.
Locks the screen at maximum brightness. When off, the system brightness setting applies.
Critical alerts raise the alarm volume to maximum, then put it back.
Beeps every few seconds while the hub can\'t be reached.
Keeps the hub connection alive when the device is unplugged.
Lets critical alerts take over the screen while another app is open.
Some brands, Samsung especially, put apps to sleep on their own. Check that Dashboardz isn\'t on that list.
Disconnects it from the hub. You\'ll need a new pairing code to connect again.
It stops showing screens and alerts until you pair it again with a new code from the hub\'s Devices page.
Swipe down with two fingers to open settings
Two Android permissions keep this device working as a wall panel. You can change them later in settings.
Tip: a two-finger swipe down opens Settings from anywhere.
This device needs a WebView update

Dashboardz draws its screens with Android System WebView. This device has version %1$d, and Dashboardz needs %2$d or newer. Update \"Android System WebView\" from the Play Store (on Android 7 to 9, update Chrome instead), then reopen Dashboardz. Without a Google account, you can install a newer WebView APK from its official source.
